texts: Welcome to Quiz Rush! It's general knowledge day! Forty photo questions: animals, places, science and more. You have ten seconds each. Ready? Let's play!
Kick-off! What is this animal?
Yes! It's Zebra. No two zebras have exactly the same stripe pattern.
Take a good look. Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
That's Mars. Its red colour comes from iron oxide, or rust, in the soil.
Easy one... or is it? Which city is famous for these canals?
It's Amsterdam. Amsterdam has more than 160 canals.
Eyes on the screen. What is the largest animal on Earth?
Correct answer: Blue whale. It can grow to about 30 metres long.
Quick! How many legs does a spider have?
Of course, it's 8. Insects have six legs, so spiders are not insects.
Trust your instinct. At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
Boom! It's 100 degrees Celsius. That's 212 degrees Fahrenheit.
Don't overthink it. Which instrument is this?
Here it is: Violin. A violin usually has four strings.
This one is a classic. What is the tallest animal in the world?
You got it, it's Giraffe. A giraffe's neck has seven bones, the same as a human's.
Here we go. Which fruit is this?
Spot on! It's Pineapple. A pineapple takes about two years to grow.
Last easy one! Which bird is this?
The answer is Flamingo. Flamingos get their pink colour from the food they eat.
Medium round! Things get trickier. What is the highest mountain on Earth?
Yes! It's Mount Everest. Its summit is about 8,849 metres above sea level.
Look closely. What is the capital of Turkey?
That's Ankara. Ankara became the capital of Turkey in 1923.
Ten seconds on the clock. Which gas makes up most of Earth's air?
It's Nitrogen. Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of the air.
This one fools a lot of people. In which country is this temple?
Correct answer: Indonesia. Borobudur is the largest Buddhist temple in the world.
Can you get this one right? Which mammal lays eggs?
Of course, it's Platypus. Platypuses and echidnas are the only mammals that lay eggs.
Think carefully. How many strings does a standard guitar have?
Boom! It's 6. Bass guitars usually have four.
Here's a tricky one. What is the largest country in the world by area?
Here it is: Russia. Russia spans eleven time zones.
Keep that streak going! Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
You got it, it's Mercury. Mercury was once used in most thermometers.
Next up. What is the longest river in South America?
Spot on! It's the Amazon. The Amazon carries more water than any other river.
Last medium question! How many teeth does an adult usually have?
The answer is 32. That includes the four wisdom teeth.
Hard round! Only the experts from here. In which country is this waterfall?
Yes! It's Venezuela. Angel Falls is the highest uninterrupted waterfall in the world.
Not so easy now. What is the capital of Brazil?
That's Brasília. Brasília was built from scratch and opened in 1960.
Here's one for the experts. Which bird can fly backwards?
It's Hummingbird. Some hummingbirds beat their wings more than 50 times a second.
Take your time... but not too much. What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
Correct answer: Na. Na comes from natrium, its Latin name.
This one is a real head-scratcher. In which country is this ancient monument?
Of course, it's the United Kingdom. Stonehenge was built around 5,000 years ago.
Big brain time! How many hearts does an octopus have?
Boom! It's 3. Its blood is blue because it is rich in copper.
Lock in your answer! Which country is home to this bird, the kiwi?
Here it is: New Zealand. The kiwi is a flightless bird about the size of a chicken.
Few people get this one. What is the largest island in the world?
You got it, it's Greenland. About 80 percent of Greenland is covered by ice.
Are you still with me? Which element are both diamonds and graphite made of?
Spot on! It's Carbon. Pencil lead is actually graphite.
Last hard one! In which country did the ancient Olympic Games begin?
The answer is Greece. The ancient Games began in Olympia in 776 BC.
Genius round! Only true masters get these. What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
Yes! It's Astana. Astana has been the capital since 1997.
Seriously tough now. Which mammal can live the longest?
That's Bowhead whale. Some bowhead whales are thought to live over 200 years.
If you know this one, you're a legend. What is the capital of Bhutan?
It's Thimphu. Thimphu is one of the few capitals with no traffic lights.
Deep cut! Which tree species grows the tallest?
Correct answer: the coast redwood. The tallest known redwood is over 115 metres high.
Here's a rare one. Which gemstone is this?
Of course, it's Emerald. Emerald is a green variety of the mineral beryl.
No hints this time. What is the capital of Myanmar?
Boom! It's Naypyidaw. Naypyidaw replaced Yangon as the capital in 2006.
Almost there! Which mammal is covered in scales?
Here it is: Pangolin. When threatened, a pangolin rolls up into a tight ball.
Only a handful of people will get this. Which city was Japan's capital for over 1,000 years?
You got it, it's Kyoto. Kyoto was the imperial capital from 794 to 1869.
Second to last! What is the largest lizard in the world?
Spot on! It's Komodo dragon. Komodo dragons can grow up to 3 metres long.
Final question! Make it count. Which country produces the most coffee?
The answer is Brazil. Brazil has been the top coffee producer for over 150 years.
That's the end! How many did you get right? Drop your score in the comments, and come back tomorrow, there's a brand new quiz every day on Quiz Rush!
